subject: Ops handshake: hosting boundary & legacy cutover plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ops handshake: hosting boundary & legacy cutover plan

Hi Simon — great to meet today. Quick written recap and clear next steps so we’re aligned on hosting and the migration path from your legacy GPU cluster. High level notes from our call: 

- Hosting preferences discussed: you said the business will prefer Private VPC for PHI-sensitive flows but the product team is open to Dedicated for an initial tiered rollout to accelerate time-to-market. Hosted API was discussed as a short-lived fallback for low-risk features.
- Traffic profile: 1M tokens/day expected after M0, with peak qps ~220 (90th pct). Latency SLO target: 150-200ms p95 for single-turn generation.
- Compliance: PHI handling, signed BAA requirement, audit log retention requested (7 years), and KMS/HSM for keys.
- Migration constraints: your models are exported as TorchScript with a custom batching proxy; the legacy cluster uses a persistent KV cache design and synchronous batching patterns.
- Risks: model format adaptations, KV cache stateful migration, request auth mapping, and QA/regression on generation outputs post-quantization.

Immediate proposed plan / asks from AegisHealth: 
1) Please confirm procurement contact (procurement@...) and target PO timeline (you mentioned "end of October / Nov 1" as a hard milestone).
2) Send an architecture sketch (diagram or notes) showing where PHI is ingested, what leaves the network, and where the legacy batching proxy sits.
3) Share a representative trace / traffic sample (anonymized) and 72-hr p95/p99 latency telemetry so we can size Dedicated pools and simulate cutover.

What Redwood will deliver this week: 
- Attached: draft Dedicated proposal with sizing and cost estimate (redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf).
- Attached: migration-checklist.xlsx — a pragmatic adapter checklist for KV/cache, model format conversion notes, and a staged cutover plan (canary -> ramp -> switch).
- We’ll scope a 2-week technical PoC on a Dedicated pool (can take an initial slice of traffic) and offer a Private VPC readiness assessment in parallel.

Next steps I propose (timeline): 
- By Mon 10/05: Aegis sends procurement contact + arch sketch + sample traces.
- By Fri 10/09: We finalize PoC scope and calendar.
- By Fri 10/23: Procurement/PO or signed SOW to secure Dedicated capacity for initial rollout.

If you’re leaning Private VPC for the start, call that out explicitly and we’ll prioritize the readiness assessment and KMS integration plan. Otherwise, we recommend Dedicated first to reduce operational friction and accelerate testing.

Thanks — I’ll book a 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra lead once we have the arch sketch.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0182
redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf (PDF, 6 pages); migration-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@aegishealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 17:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops handshake: hosting boundary & legacy cutover plan

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and constraints from our side: 

- Priority: PHI handling is non-negotiable. Our legal and security teams will require Private VPC + BAA for any production workload that touches EHR data. However, we are open to a two-phase approach: (1) Dedicated for non-PHI features (chat assists and search) to accelerate time-to-value; (2) Private VPC for PHI-sensitive flows.
- Procurement: procurement@aegishealth.com is the right mailbox; I’ve looped them in. PO target: Nov 1 is correct — that’s driven by fiscal Q4 planning.
- Legacy details: models are TorchScript artifacts; bespoke batching proxy handles sequence bucketing and some request-side token normalization. We will need an adapter for the KV cache or a way to persist/restore cache state across the cutover — otherwise warm-up costs will be painful.
- Security survey: link to our security questionnaire (internal): https://aegishealth.sharepoint.com/security/questionnaire — security will expect SOC2 Type II and a short architecture/data flow diagram.

I’ve attached a short note from our infra lead about sequence bucketing and where the proxy sits relative to the model server. We can do a tech call next week — Tue/Wed mornings PST work.

Simon
Simon Bryant
Principal Infra Engineer, AegisHealth
simon.bryant@aegishealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@aegishealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 10:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops handshake: hosting boundary & legacy cutover plan

Simon / Diego — looping in a short security + procurement checklist so we can accelerate the Private VPC readiness path in parallel with the Dedicated PoC. I attached the redwood-security-pack.pdf that includes our SOC2 attestations, KMS integrations, and audit log retention options.

Minimum items security will request for Private VPC / PHI: 
- Signed BAA (we have a standard BAA template; legal can fast-track once we have PO/SOW).
- SOC2 Type II report (attached).
- Architecture/data flow diagram (redacted ok for initial review).
- KMS integration plan (customer-managed key supported).
- Access controls: list of admin personnel + IP allowlist for management plane.
- Retention & deletion policy for logs/evidences.

Procurement notes: 
- If you want Dedicated first, we can provide a 30-day committed window SOW to reserve capacity while Private VPC onboarding completes.
- We’ll prepare a short SOW that covers a 2-week PoC, including engineering hours for the KV adapter (estimated 40h).

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive with infra lead: Tue 10/06 09:00–10:00 PDT or Wed 10/07 11:00–12:00 PDT. Please confirm preferred slot.

— Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-security-pack.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bryant <simon.bryant@aegishealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:22:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops handshake: hosting boundary & legacy cutover plan

Thanks Simon / Monica — confirming next steps and owners: 

- Simon / Aegis: send architecture sketch + anonymized sample traces by EOD Mon 10/05 (owner: Simon).
- Procurement: confirm PO timeline and any procurement templates (owner: procurement@aegishealth.com).
- Redwood: we’ll send a formal SOW + DocuSign link for the 2-week Dedicated PoC and adapter engineering work by EOD 10/05 (owner: Diego). Link: https://docusign.net/InitSOW/DG-9342.
- Security: Monica to provide SOC2 + KMS integration docs (owner: Monica).
- Schedule: technical deep-dive Tue 10/06 09:00 PDT — I’ll set the invite after Simon confirms.

We’ll include a fallback plan to route low-risk feature traffic to Redwood Hosted API for a limited percentage during cutover if you want a warm ramp while Private VPC is standing up.

I’ve attached the two files I referenced earlier and will follow up with the SOW. If all good, I’ll prepare the PO-ready SOW that procurement can sign and return.

Best —
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
